findings.text: §22's deliverable says "One definition remains, in `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py`, and `reports.py` imports it" but names no import site, and the pair is already an import cycle: `reckon/crew/promotion_evidence.py:22` imports `reckon.crew.reports` at module scope (`_NONE_VALUES`, `parse_manifest`), `reckon/crew/promotion.py:2242` imports `promotion_evidence` at module scope, and `reports.py` defines `parse_manifest` far below its import block, so a top-of-file `from reckon.crew.promotion_evidence import _commit_resolves_in` raises ImportError in both initialization orders; the implementer must instead defer the import to the call site (as `reckon/crew/reports.py:2097` already does for `_resolve_commit`) or place it after reports.py's definitions, and the section should say which, since its negative control ("the citation tests in both modules fail on import") presumes the module-level form that the required deferred form will not produce
